earlier.title: The paper EDITOR surface and root.html.heex declare DIFFERENT serif stacks — every ch number in this epic is Iowan because of it
earlier.description:
MEASURED LIVE by scripts/studio-desk-measure.mjs against guerrilla @ 0b4c677fdb88caa1238095cc5cbe4f624a4d65dc (slot blue). getComputedStyle('.bp-paper-surface').fontFamily inside the Studio editor resolves to: "Iowan Old Style", "Palatino Linotype", Palatino, Charter, Georgia, 'Source Serif 4', serif — which comes from api/assets/paper-editor/src/styles.css (and the identical line in api/assets/paper-surface/paper-surface.css), NOT from root.html.heex, whose --paper-font-serif reads 'Source Serif 4', Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif. Two sheets, one token name, different values; the editor's wins.

WHY IT MATTERS. spd-s5 self-hosted Source Serif 4 specifically so non-macOS users get a known face, and root.html.heex was repointed to lead with it — but on the surface that actually matters the self-hosted face is SIXTH in the stack and never wins on macOS. Every native-face number this epic holds (10.000px/ch, 64.00ch at viewport 900) is Iowan Old Style, a face that exists on Apple platforms and essentially nowhere else. A Linux or Windows reader falls through to Charter/Georgia/Source Serif 4 and gets a materially different measure: forced Georgia reads 11.0469px/ch (57.93ch at 900px) and forced Source Serif 4 reads 9.1719px/ch (69.78ch) — a 20% spread on the number the epic's headline criterion is stated in.

NOT A REGRESSION and not fixed here: this is the same class as spd-b25-bulldocs-reader-gutter-desync. Decide deliberately which stack the reading surface should declare, unify the two sites, and re-run the instrument to re-baseline every ch figure. Sibling risk: whichever face leads changes what calc(55ch + 80px) resolves to (630.591px Iowan / 687.632px Georgia / 584.897px Source Serif 4), which directly moves whether the floor binds — see spd-b28.

later.title: root.html.heex and the built paper-editor CSS declare DIFFERENT serif stacks, and the winner decides every ch figure in this epic
later.description:
root.html.heex declares --paper-font-serif as "Source Serif 4", Georgia, Times New Roman, serif — Source Serif 4 FIRST. The built api/priv/static/assets/bp-paper-editor.css (from api/assets/paper-editor/src/styles.css) declares .bp-paper-surface font-family via --tok-reading-font as Iowan Old Style, Palatino Linotype, Palatino, Charter, Georgia, Source Serif 4, serif — Iowan FIRST and Source Serif 4 SIXTH. The editor sheet wins, which is why every native-face number this epic holds (10.0000 px/ch, 64.00ch at viewport 900) is IOWAN — a face that exists essentially only on Apple platforms. Non-Apple readers fall through to Charter or Georgia (11.0469 px/ch, 57.93ch at 900) long before reaching the self-hosted Source Serif 4 that spd-s5 exists to ship (9.1719 px/ch, 69.78ch). That is a ~20% spread on the number the epic headline criterion is stated in. The FORCED per-face rows in the instrument bypass the cascade and are unaffected, and the charter correctly labels its native rows Iowan — so no published figure is wrong. What is wrong is the claim that the self-hosted face protects cross-platform readers: it does not, until these two stacks agree. Sibling of spd-w5-bulldocs-gutter-desync (same class: the public reader has its own separate literal gutter declaration the Studio floor never reads).

Slug uniqueness cannot catch this class; only a content read can (recorded on spd-b40-ledger-short-number-collisions). spd-b27 is CANCELLED as duplicate-of this task, which survives as the sharper statement (it correctly notes the FORCED per-face rows bypass the cascade and the charter labels its native rows Iowan, so no published figure is wrong — b27 implied a full re-baseline that is not owed).

FOLDED IN FROM spd-b27, the detail this task lacked and which must not be lost:
  - The third declaration site: api/assets/paper-surface/paper-surface.css carries the SAME Iowan-first line as api/assets/paper-editor/src/styles.css. Any reconciliation must touch BOTH, not just the editor sheet, or the surfaces re-diverge.
  - THE SIBLING RISK, which is why this is not cosmetic: whichever face leads changes what calc(55ch + 80px) RESOLVES to — 630.591px Iowan / 687.632px Georgia / 584.897px Source Serif 4 — and that directly moves whether the protected floor binds. See spd-b28-floor-binds-georgia-1280-overflow. Changing the declared stack is therefore a LAYOUT change, not a typography preference.
  - Class sibling: spd-b25-bulldocs-reader-gutter-desync / spd-w5-bulldocs-gutter-desync — one token name, two sheets, different values, the surface that matters wins silently.
  - spd-s5 self-hosted Source Serif 4 so non-macOS readers get a KNOWN face; at position six in the stack it never wins on macOS and rarely elsewhere. That intent is currently unrealised.
